class.name: FellowInteriorMaterial3D
class.brief_description: FellowEngine: window glass with a room behind it — interior mapping (milestone 188).
class.description: A material for windows' glass that shows a room behind each window without its geometry: the view's ray is followed into a box (its side walls, floor, ceiling and back wall), whatever it meets drawn there — the walls' plaster or paper, panelling, a skirting and a cornice; on the back wall a painting, a door (shut, or open on the dark of the next room), a bookcase or a wardrobe; pictures on the side walls; cotto tiles, boards, a parquet or stone on the floor, and a rug; wooden beams across the ceiling or plaster; furniture across the middle of the room (a table with chairs and a vase, a sofa, an armchair with a lamp beside it, a desk) and in front of the back wall (a sideboard with a lamp or a vase on it, a bed's head); a lamp hanging from the ceiling; curtains just behind the glass (drapes drawn to either side, or a net). Each window's room is another, chosen by a hash of where its room is in the mesh and [member seed]. The rooms are lit by the day through the window, falling off into them ([member daylight], [member daylight_color]), and, in [member lamp_share] of them, by their lamp ([member lamp_energy], [member lamp_color]); all of it seen through the glass by Fresnel's law, with grime, the sky's reflection ([member reflection]) and old panes a little out of true ([member pane_size]). Where the rooms are: with [member rooms_from_uv2] each window has its own, centred on it, from the glass's UV2 — the metres right of the window's middle (along the facade: the up axis crossed with the glass's normal) and up from its room's floor (for a window with a sill, 0.9 m under its bottom). With it off, the facade is cut into rooms [member room_size] wide and high from [member floor_height], in the mesh's space. Glass facing up or down shows no room. One shader for every instance, made once. See [code]docs/decisions/0330-rooms-behind-the-windows.md[/code].

members.member: The share of windows with curtains: of them six in ten drapes drawn to either side, four a net across the glass. A window whose glass's vertex colour has an alpha under 0.5 (a shop's window, a door's glass) has none.

How bright the rooms are by day, near the window: the light falls off into the room, to a tenth at its back wall, and less into its corners. The rooms glow with it (it is not the scene's light): lower it at dusk, to [code]0.05[/code] or so at night, when [member lamp_share] lights some.
The day's light's colour in the rooms.
With [member rooms_from_uv2] off: the height of a storey's floor in the mesh's space (the storeys [member room_size]'s height apart from it).
How furnished the rooms are: [code]1[/code] eight in ten rooms with furniture across the middle and half with some against the back wall; [code]0[/code] none.
The glass's roughness (more where it is grimy).
The colour the glass gives what is seen through it.
How dirty the glass is: dimmer and rougher in patches.
How bright a lit lamp is, and the room round it.
The share of rooms whose hanging lamp is lit (the others' hangs dark).

The size of a window's panes in metres (in its UV2's frame): each pane's normal a little out of true, as old glass is, so that the reflections break at its edges. [code]Vector2(0, 0)[/code]: flat glass.
How much of the sky the glass mirrors (the environment's reflection, occluded by this much: a street's other houses hide most of the sky a window would mirror).
A room's width (along the facade), height and depth (into the building), in metres.
Each window its own room from its glass's UV2 (above). Off: a grid of rooms along the facade in the mesh's space ([member room_size], [member floor_height]), a window possibly looking into two.
Another set of rooms for the same windows.
